data.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued November 4 at 3:23AM EST until November 4 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Statement, isolated minor coastal
flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Broward County and Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Statement, through Wednesday
evening. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Wednesday
morning.

* IMPACTS...Some water on low lying roads and property. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water. Minor coastal flooding is possible within 1.5 to
2 hours of high tide.
data.instruction:
Do not drive through flooded roadways.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

FXUS62 KMFL 041130
AFDMFL

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Miami FL
630 AM EST Wed Nov 4 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 630 AM EST Wed Nov 4 2026

  - Additional rainfall could result in localized flooding across
    portions of the area that have seen repeated rounds of heavy
    rainfall over the last several days. Highest chances during
    the morning hours over the Atlantic coast. 

  - Minor coastal flooding expected during times of high tide.

  - Dangerous beach conditions are expected across the Atlantic
    coast through today.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Thursday)
Issued at 315 AM EST Wed Nov 4 2026

Overnight period has remained busy radar-wise with persisting 
training of cells around northern Broward county. Flash Flood 
warnings/Flood Advisories have been necessary for those areas, with 
some potential for additional showers through sunrise.   

Ensembles and global models show developing high pressure across the 
SE U.S. coast slowly moving closer to the area. This will decrease 
pressure gradients across Soflo and allow for coastal winds to 
gradually decrease starting today. Drier air is also expected to 
continue to filter into the region, which will also help in the 
downward trend of active weather. In terms of POPs, latest NBM keeps 
highest values through the mid morning hours, mainly over the 
immediate Atlantic coastal areas of SoFlo where up to 80% for that 
time period. WPC is also keeping a Marginal Risk for Excesssive 
Rainfall (level 1 of 4), mainly for the morning hours.  

The high pressure will continue to inch closer to the area on 
Thursday, with a more pronounced mid-lvl layer of drier air 
establishing across SoFlo. This will result in POPs dropping into
single digits by the afternoon hours, and widespread light to 
moderate NE flow. Meanwhile, a sfc dry front will begin moving 
across the state, with reinforcing high pressure in its wake. 
 
Also, coastal hazards continue as high astronomical tides combine 
with persistent onshore winds to keep threat of coastal flooding in 
place today. 

Afternoon temperatures will remain in the mid to upper 80s each day, 
with slightly warmer values on Thursday with more hours of 
sunshine. 

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Thursday night through Tuesday)
Issued at 315 AM EST Wed Nov 4 2026

Long range models depict reinforcing high pressure and drier 
conditions prevailing across the area during the weekend in the wake 
of a dry FROPA. Mainly single-digit POPs are expected each day 
through Sunday. 

For early next week, models depict a potential mid-lvl trough moving 
across the area and bringing increasing chances of showers for the 
late Monday-Tuesday timeframe. But even so, max POPs seem to remain 
in the 20-30% range. 

The latest trend in guidance is also to bring a more pronounced 
temperature response as overall northerly flow develops in the 
wake of the FROPA. Afternoon highs should remain in the upper 70s 
to low 80s by early next week. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 630 AM EST Wed Nov 4 2026

Winds will remain generally NE in the 10-12kt range through around
00Z, then L/V tonight. Some brief MVFR/IFR cigs/vis periods are
still possible this morning over the Atlantic terminals with 
coastal showers and thunderstorms. Mainly VFR conditions should 
prevail later in the day. 

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 315 AM EST Wed Nov 4 2026

Marine conditions will continue to gradually improve across the 
Atlantic waters as winds subside, and a more gentle NE flow
develops. Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms will 
continue across all Atlantic waters, with highest chances during
the morning hours, while mainly isolated showers prevail over the
Gulf waters today. Significantly drier conditions will prevail
during the weekend in the wake of a dry frontal passage across the
region. 

&&

.BEACHES...
Issued at 315 AM EST Wed Nov 4 2026

The onshore flow will keep a High Risk for rip currents across 
Atlantic beaches for one more day, then conditions begin improving
tonight. Higher than usual tides will also continue to keep 
elevated water levels near the coast today. 

&&

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
100 PM EST Wed Nov 4 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Western and Central Atlantic:
A non-tropical low pressure area is located a few hundred miles 
south of Bermuda.  Environmental conditions could support this 
system gradually acquiring subtropical characteristics through this 
weekend while it moves slowly eastward over the western and central 
subtropical Atlantic.  By early next week, environmental conditions 
are forecast to become unfavorable for further development.  For 
more information on this system, including Gale Warnings, please see 
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service. 
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...30 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service can be 
found under AWIPS header NFDHSFAT1, WMO header FZNT01 KWBC, and 
online at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFAT1.php

$$
